Where it's headed and the principles that steer it

Vision

principles · safety floor · closed loop

The Product Spec Harness is opinionated by design. Every flag, every rule, every limit traces back to a small set of principles chosen to keep a non-technical product owner in control of their own spec — and keep the AI from taking shortcuts that erode that control. This page documents those principles, the always-on safety floor, and the feedback loop they make possible.

The operating contract

Five operating principles

These five principles are stated verbatim in CLAUDE.md and govern every turn — not just when a skill is loaded. They resolve the ambiguity that anti-rationalization shortcuts exploit.

1 — Frontmatter is source-of-truth

Parse YAML; never infer structure from headings. The spec hierarchy lives in structured frontmatter, not in prose. A heading can be edited without changing the spec's meaning; the YAML fields cannot be.

2 — DRY — one home per fact

Cross-reference by ID; never duplicate prose. A goal stated in the BRD is referenced from child PRDs by its ID (BRD-G1), not copied. Copied prose drifts; IDs don't.

3 — Script vs LLM split — scripts handle graph/struct; LLM judges prose/alignment. Scripts first.

Deterministic scripts catch orphans, broken trace, missing AC, ID integrity. The LLM layer adds what scripts cannot: INVEST quality, vagueness, core-value drift, contradiction. Running scripts first keeps the gate reproducible; the LLM layer is advisory and never gates CI alone.

4 — Never overwrite PO prose

On --update, flag affected nodes and ask before regenerating. The product owner's wording is their intent. Silently tidying it up substitutes the AI's judgment for theirs. Flag, then ask — always.

5 — No silent reversals

A new claim that contradicts an approved artifact is a stop point — not an auto-fix. Three choices are surfaced: Keep (reject the new claim) · Change (re-approve with owner + date) · Hybrid (record both, schedule follow-up). Only the PO choosing Change with explicit re-approval touches approved content. See the Decision Register for how rulings are recorded.

⚠️ Anti-rationalization — shortcuts these principles close off
  • "Let me just write the code" → Spec tool. Capture story + AC for the build team.
  • "Scope is obvious, I'll set it" → Scope is the PO's call. Never assume — ask.
  • "Contradicts approved, I'll fix it" → Surface Keep / Change / Hybrid. Never silently flip.
  • "Clear to mark approved" → Needs explicit PO approval + owner + date.
  • "I'll tidy their wording" → Never overwrite PO prose. Flag, then ask.
Non-negotiable, every turn

The always-on safety floor

Two GATEs in CLAUDE.md apply on every single turn — they do not depend on a skill being loaded, a reference file being in context, or a PO having opted in. They are the floor below which the harness never operates.

GATE-NO-SILENT-REVERSAL

A new claim that contradicts an approved artifact is a stop point. Do not edit, pick a side, or tidy it up. Surface verbatim with three choices: Keep (reject new claim) · Change (re-approve, owner + date) · Hybrid (record both, follow-up). Only the PO choosing Change with explicit re-approval touches approved content. If unsure it truly contradicts — ask. Record the ruling in the Decision Register (DEC-<n>) so it is not re-litigated.

GATE-NEVER-ASSUME

Ask by default. Assume only when: the PO already answered (.session.md / PRODUCT.md); a closed allowed-value field has exactly one fit; or generating PO-editable boilerplate (and you say so). Never assume persona identities/counts, core-value alignment, scope (in / out / core-value), or sign-off. Never set status: approved without explicit PO approval + owner + date. In doubt about assuming — you're not. Ask.

These GATEs cannot be waived — not even if the PO says "skip asking." If the PO requests that, proceed, but name the residual risk. The gates themselves never switch off.

Spec → build → measure → learn

The closed loop

The four skills are not independent tools — they form a pipeline with a return edge. A critique report flows back into the spec via --apply-critique, turning findings into recorded decisions. Usage data flows back via telemetry, showing which skills run and which stall. The --learn flag closes the full loop: spec → build → measure → learn.

Define → Validate → Critique

product-spec builds the hierarchy; --validate proves it is structurally sound; product-spec-critique says whether it is actually good — and why it might die. The critique report ends with concrete fixes, not free-floating insults.

Critique → Decisions (--apply-critique)

A finding becomes a DEC-<n> entry in the Decision Register only when the PO confirms it. --apply-critique <report> walks through each finding and asks. Nothing is auto-accepted. See Decision Register for the full ruling format.

Approved spec → Ship (release)

Once the spec is approved and critiques resolved, release packs the harness itself — skills, agents, hooks, rules, eval-gate — into a versioned, byte-identical tar.gz. CI builds are tag-triggered; SHA-256 sidecars prove integrity. See release.

Observe → Learn (telemetry)

telemetry closes the loop with read-only usage and health data — which skills ran, which scripts errored, whether sub-agents succeeded. It reports whether the machinery runs, never whether the product wins the market. Every report ends with a mandatory "what this does NOT measure" section. See telemetry.

The full journey — from first install through a spec, critique, and shipped release — is walked step by step in the journey guide.

Plain language · offline · open

Built for product owners

No code required

Every skill is invoked with a single /cleanmatic:* command. The interview, validation, critique, and reports all happen in plain language. The PO never touches a terminal, a YAML file, or a Python script directly.

Bilingual EN / VI

Every skill accepts --lang en or --lang vi. The interview, generated prose, visualization labels, and critique reports all render in the chosen language. IDs and frontmatter keys stay English so the structure is stable across languages. Vietnamese phrasing is native-reviewed for natural wording.

Offline after install

All four skills make no network calls at runtime. Your spec, your telemetry data, and your critique reports stay on your machine. The one-time installer vendors the JS runtimes and verifies each with a pinned SHA-256. See the rig — runs offline for the full privacy guarantee.
